events.text: Rumi on Silence: The Lesson of the Quiet Ones
events.sub: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation

events.text: Rumi wrote more than sixty thousand lines of poetry, and he kept telling himself to be quiet.
Many of his ghazals end with one word: khamush. Silence.
Here are eight passages about the wisdom that lives beyond words.

events.fa: چه قبله کرده‌ای این گفت و گو را
events.en: Why have you made all this talk your direction of prayer?

events.fa: طلب کن درس خاموشان کدام است
events.en: Go and find out: what is the lesson of the silent ones?

events.text: A qibla is the direction you face when you pray.
Rumi asks: why have you turned toward talking, as if it were sacred?
There is a school where the silent ones teach.
Their lesson cannot be explained. It can only be learned by becoming quiet.

fa: چه قبله کرده‌ای این گفت و گو را
طلب کن درس خاموشان کدام است

events.fa: با لب دمساز خود گر جفتمی
events.en: If I were joined to the lips of my true companion,
I too, like the reed, would say all that can be said.

events.fa: هر که او از همزبانی شد جدا
events.en: Whoever is parted from one who speaks their language

events.fa: بی‌زبان شد گر چه دارد صد نوا
events.en: becomes tongueless, though they have a hundred songs.

events.text: A reed flute only sings when it touches the lips of the one who plays it.
Rumi says he is like that.
Some silences are not empty. They are the silence of someone who has no one to speak to.
When we find the person who speaks our language, the songs come back.

fa: با لب دمساز خود گر جفتمی
هر که او از همزبانی شد جدا
بی‌زبان شد گر چه دارد صد نوا

events.fa: در نیابد حال پخته هیچ خام
events.en: The raw cannot grasp the state of the ripe;
so the words must be brief. Farewell.

events.text: Rumi often divides people into the raw and the cooked, the unripe and the ripe.
Some things can only be understood by living them.
Explaining them to someone who has not lived them is like describing a taste.
So he stops. Not out of pride, but out of honesty.

fa: در نیابد حال پخته هیچ خام

events.fa: به سوزنی که دهان‌ها بدوخت در رمضان
events.en: With the needle that sewed mouths shut in Ramadan,

events.fa: بیا بدوز دهانم که سیرم از گفتار
events.en: come, sew my mouth, for I am full of talking.

events.text: During Ramadan, mouths close to food and drink from dawn to dusk.
Rumi asks for a different fast: a fast from words.
He says he is full, the way one is full after too much bread.
Sometimes the soul needs to stop speaking the way the body needs to stop eating.

fa: به سوزنی که دهان‌ها بدوخت در رمضان
بیا بدوز دهانم که سیرم از گفتار

events.fa: بس کن و چون ماهیان باش خموش اندر آب
events.en: Enough. Be silent, like the fish in the water,

events.fa: تا نه چو تابه شود بر سر نارم طواف
events.en: so that my circling does not end like a pan's, turning over the fire.

events.text: Fish live in water, and they live in silence.
In this ghazal Rumi has been circling the beloved, like pilgrims circling the Kaaba.
He warns himself: too many words, and the circling turns into frying over a fire.
Stay in the water. Stay quiet. That is where life is.

fa: بس کن و چون ماهیان باش خموش اندر آب
تا نه چو تابه شود بر سر نارم طواف

events.fa: ای ناطقه بر بام و در تا کی روی در خانه پر
events.en: O speaking soul, how long will you wander over roof and door? Fly into the house.

events.fa: نطق زبان را ترک کن بی‌چانه شو بی‌چانه شو
events.en: Leave the speech of the tongue. Be without a jaw, be without a jaw.

events.text: The speaking part of us is restless. It runs over rooftops and knocks on doors.
Rumi tells it to fly inside, into the house of the heart.
His image is almost funny: become jawless.
There is a way of knowing that does not need the mouth at all.

fa: ای ناطقه بر بام و در تا کی روی در خانه پر
نطق زبان را ترک کن بی‌چانه شو بی‌چانه شو

events.fa: ای دل ز خود چو باخبری رو خموش کن
events.en: O heart, since you know yourself, go and be silent;

events.fa: چون بی‌خبر مباش به اخبار آمده
events.en: do not be like the unknowing, who arrive full of news.

events.text: Those who know little often have the most to say.
Rumi tells his heart: you have tasted something. Now be quiet about it.
Real knowledge of the self tends to make people gentler and quieter.
The news-bringers are loud. The ones who know are still.

fa: ای دل ز خود چو باخبری رو خموش کن
چون بی‌خبر مباش به اخبار آمده

events.fa: بیهوده چند گویی خاموش کن بس است
events.en: How long will you talk in vain? Be silent. It is enough.

events.fa: فرمان گفت نیست همان گیر که الکنی
events.en: There is no command to speak. Imagine you were a stammerer.

events.text: Rumi often closes a poem by scolding himself like this.
No one ordered him to speak. He could simply stop.
Imagine, he says, that you could not get the words out at all.
And so we end where he would want us to end: in silence.

fa: بیهوده چند گویی خاموش کن بس است
فرمان گفت نیست همان گیر که الکنی

events.text: Thank you for staying with these verses.
Every week we share real passages of Rumi, translated honestly from the Persian.
